newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The company building the Yadana gas pipeline has petitioned Her Majesty the Queen in an attempt to have the project re-routed. Prasit Supsakorn, chairman of the Tasco Mannesmann joint venture, has written to the Bureau of the Royal Household on March 24, suggesting an alternative route along highways. (BANGKOK POST) (BUSINESS DAY)

- Coalition parties led by Chart Pattana has torpedoed the Interior Ministry's attempt to seek 94 billion baht in tied-over funding to build and improve rural roads. At its weekly meeting yesterday, the interior minister and his deputy urged the cabinet to approve the Accelerated Rural Development Office's plan to upgrade 20,000 km of roads as envisaged by the Highways Department. The Interior Ministry had sought 94 billion baht, spread over five years, for the purpose. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Interior Ministry has set up a high-level committee to closely monitor news reports in an attempt by the government to effectively counter media criticism. A source says that the committee, established by Interior Minister Snoh Thienthong at the request of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, will monitor news reports that are critical of the ministry and the government. (THE NATION)

- Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has hinted that the government might take back the banking licences awarded to the Italian Thai-led and MBK-led consortiums following an apparent lack of progress since receiving them. He says that only the consortium led by General Finance and Securities Plc has shown its readiness to operate a bank within a year after being awarded its licence, as required by the financial authorities. (THE NATION)

- British Steel Plc, the world's third largest steel producer, is studying a plan to invest an additional 4 billion baht to 5 billion baht in the Asia-Pacific, with Thailand a likely target country for investments to serve the automotive and other industries. Thailand is being compared with other priority countries, including Indonesia and southern China. (THE NATION)
